title: Deployment choreography and fallback playbooks for hybrid environments
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: We need a single declarative choreography for model promotions that runs across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments while respecting environment-specific constraints (networking, KMS, capacity, and air-gapped policies). Current rollouts are fragmented: hosted supports rapid shadowing and A/B splitters, Dedicated has reserved pools and burst policies, and some Private customers prohibit external telemetry or shadow traffic. This ticket defines a policy-driven choreography and a set of fallback playbooks that controllers and the Console can enact during canaries, A/B tests, and auto-rollbacks.

Goals: 
- Define a declarative 'choreography' object (YAML/JSON) that describes stages (shadow -> canary -> ramp -> cutover) and permissible actions per environment.
- Implement guardrails that prevent unsupported actions in Private (e.g., cross-VPC shadowing) and provide deterministic fallbacks (e.g., local metrics-only gating).
- Extend control plane to synthesize per-environment execution plans at deploy-time and expose a diff in the Console.
- Provide a runbook and automated rollback playbooks triggered by metric thresholds, errors, or human aborts.

Constraints and environment-specific notes: 
- Hosted: supports full feature set (shadow, weighting, multi-variant A/B, cross-region mirroring). We can use telemetry and off-host analysis.
- Dedicated: supports shadowing within the same customer pool but requires capacity checks; autoscale policies may delay promotion.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): often disallows outbound data and cross-network shadowing; only local metric collectors and webhook-based notifications are allowed. Some customers require air-gapped approval before auto-rollback.

Risk areas: 
- Inconsistent rollback semantics across tiers may surprise customers; runbooks must be explicit.
- Telemetry gaps in Private mean some auto-rollback triggers must be conservative to avoid false positives.

Proposal summary: 
1) Choreography schema: new top-level object with stages, guards, success criteria, and fallback strategy references. Schema will include an environmentCapabilities section that the control plane will resolve.
2) Execution planner: a control-plane service that takes choreography + target environment -> plan (sequence of steps) and exposes a dry-run. Plans are annotated with blockedReasons when actions are disallowed.
3) Rollback playbooks: templated reversible actions (scale down model, re-route traffic, invalidate caches) and an auto-rollback engine that evaluates short-window SLOs plus long-window quality regressions.
4) Console UX: show per-stage telemetry, allowed actions, and an audit-friendly timeline. Provide a one-click emergency rollback that runs the selected playbook.

Outcomes: unified, auditable promotions across environments; reduced incidents from misconfigured rollouts; clear customer-facing documentation on what behaviors differ by tier.
acceptance_criteria:
- Choreography schema (draft) checked into repo: docs/choreography/schema.yaml and validated by unit tests.
- Planner service implements environment capability resolution and returns a dry-run plan for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
- Console shows dry-run plan and flags blocked actions for Private deployments.
- At least one end-to-end demo: shadow -> canary -> 50% ramp -> full cutover in Hosted with automated rollback triggered by HTTP error rate threshold.
- Rollback playbooks implemented for these actions: traffic-reroute, replica-scale, model-pin; playbooks documented in runbook.
- Security review completed for Private fallback behaviors.
- Automated integration tests that simulate missing telemetry and validate conservative rollback decisions for Private.
implementation_notes:
- Schema: add /choreography/v1 schema in repo (runtime-configs). Keep schema flat (no env-specific nested objects) to simplify diffing; environment capabilities resolved externally.
- Planner: new service planner/lightweight stateless API. It must call environment capability service (env-cap) to get allowedActions. Planner returns steps with IDs to allow interruption/rollback.
- Control plane: extend deploy API with choreography_id and dry_run flag. On apply, control plane persists plan and emits audit events.
- Runtime agents: minimal changes for hosted agents to accept shadow routing headers. Dedicated agents will require scheduler-side capacity check hooks. Private agents need a local-only metrics adapter and webhook hooks for notifications.
- Telemetry: define a telemetry contract for gating metrics (latency_p50,p95,error_rate,quality_score) and ensure offline/edge collectors for Private.
- Console: add new 'Promotion plan' panel showing stage timeline, blocked reasons, and playbook links. Add a red 'Emergency rollback' CTA that runs the selected playbook via the control plane.
- Rollback engine: support both threshold-based and manual-triggered rollbacks. Implement exponential backoff for repeated rollbacks to avoid oscillations.

updates: 2026-02-17: Kickoff meeting with PM, Design, Runtime, and Console teams. Agreed to keep schema environment-agnostic and resolve capabilities at plan time.
2026-02-22: Draft choreography schema posted (see repo PR). Runtime team requested clearer IDs per step for rollback correlation.

2026-03-01: Security review triage: Private fallback requiring webhook notifications flagged for manual approval for air-gapped customers. Decision: auto-rollback allowed only when local metrics cross critical thresholds; otherwise, create an 'approval required' event.

2026-03-04: Planner PoC implemented returning dry-run plans for Hosted and Dedicated. Private plan returns 'blocked' for cross-network shadowing; suggested fallback is 'local-shadow' (collect metrics but do not mirror traffic off-host).
2026-03-08: Console mock reviewed by Design; requested inline explanation of why actions are blocked per environment (UX task created for DES-2145).
2026-03-10: Integration test harness for Private telemetry simulation added to CI. Observed false-positive rollback in a noisy test; adjusted smoothing window from 30s to 120s for Private plans.
Next steps: finish planner idempotency guarantees, wire rollback engine to audit/event pipeline, and schedule an end-to-end demo in cycle 2026-W10.
